title: Nodics Glossary
readerIntent: Use consistent business and technical meanings across Nodics documentation, code, operations, and BackOffice.
summary: These definitions prefer capability and user-outcome language; internal module names appear only where they identify implementation ownership.

sections.heading: Platform and structure
items: Nodics: a modular, governed, API-driven backend framework and application factory; it does not contain customer-facing or BackOffice frontend code.
Capability: a business or platform outcome with an explicit owner, contract, configuration, lifecycle, security, operations, tests, and documentation.
Module: the smallest package-defined ownership and extension boundary loaded by Nodics.
Module group: an organizational package that expands related modules; it is not automatically a deployable process.
Project module: a customer/application-owned later layer containing business behavior that must not be added to reusable framework modules.
Layered customization: overriding or extending an earlier definition through a later active module or governed configuration without editing released source.
Authority: the one source/service responsible for deciding and mutating a contract. Clients, caches, projections, registries, and tools do not become parallel authorities.

sections.heading: Runtime and deployment
items: Environment: a deployable topology root such as local, development, QA, pre-production, or production.
Server: one runnable process composition hosting selected active modules; a server does not own the capabilities it hosts.
Node: an optional instance-specific child of a server for coordinates, identity, capacity, scheduling, or worker responsibility.
Canonical runtime identity: the environment/server/node identity derived at runtime from validated parent ancestry, not handwritten names.
activeModules: the local process activation contract deciding which module contributions load.
servers.*: endpoint coordinates for local or remote module communication; entries do not activate modules.
MonoServer: a consolidated local/reference process used for rapid integration; it is not proof of distributed production readiness.
Modular topology: capability modules hosted across separate processes so communication, credentials, failures, scale, and lifecycle boundaries are real.
Liveness: evidence that a process exists. Readiness: evidence that it may accept new work. Draining: bounded rejection of new work while in-flight work and resources close.

sections.heading: Identity and governance
items: Tenant: the isolation and configuration scope resolved before identity and business operations.
Enterprise: a governed business organization within the supported tenant model.
Employee: a human business/BackOffice principal. Customer: a human consumer principal. Service principal: a non-human module, integration, or controlled scheduled-process identity.
Authentication: proof of caller identity and credential validity. Authorization: the target operation's decision that the principal may act.
Permission: a catalogued action grant composed through validated groups. Ownership: record-level constraint limiting principals to permitted data.
Runtime governance: preview, request, approval, activation, audit, cleanup, and rollback for supported mutable contracts.
Control plane: secured configuration, registry, diagnostics, lifecycle, and governance operations; it is not the business data path.
Data plane: normal module APIs and services that execute owned business operations.

sections.heading: Data, processes, and integration
items: Schema: the source definition for an item model, fields, relationships, access, validation, cache/event/transaction, generation, and persistence behavior.
Item model: runtime object and generated model contract derived from a schema. Search model: the corresponding query/search contract; it does not replace the item authority.
Provider-neutral contract: a stable Nodics capability interface that callers use without knowing the selected vendor adapter.
Provider adapter: a module that implements a database, cache, search, messaging, AI, storage, identity, notification, payment, or other external technology behind its neutral contract.
Pipeline: bounded ordered technical execution inside an operation. Workflow: durable business process composed of actions that may be manual or automatic.

Event: a typed/versioned fact or trigger after an authoritative transition. Messaging: transport/delivery of that fact. NEMS: persisted event definition, distribution, log, retry, and recovery capability.
CronJob: persisted time/manual trigger and scheduler lifecycle; the target service retains business behavior.
Staged: editable versioned authoring authority. Online: separate deployed, normally non-versioned serving authority.
Publication: the nPublish-governed validation, approval consumption, activation, audit, reconciliation, and rollback lifecycle that deploys an exact approved version.

sections.heading: Applications and documentation
items: Axis: reusable employee-only BackOffice web client; each customer project has its own deployment and Axis contains no backend business logic.
BackOffice backend: registry/control-plane capability that discovers active modules; Axis then calls the owning modules directly.
Storefront: backend capability resolving website/Site/Store/catalog/channel context; it is not a frontend application.
nodicsdocs: canonical structured documentation content-pack repository imported through Nodics CMS contracts and rendered by Axis or Nodicsweb.
Canonical page: approved structured source in nodicsdocs/source/pages with stable code, route, audience, order, evidence, and implementation-aligned content.
Module README: concise technical entrypoint for local ownership, setup, extension, operations, tests, and links; it is not a duplicate public user guide.
root docs/: temporary uncommitted planning/checklist space unless explicitly promoted; it is not runtime documentation authority.
